daily.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
daily.summary: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

daily.title: France suspends use of stun grenades against protesters
daily.summary: France is suspending the use of stun grenades against protesters as allegations of student brutality draw more anger. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is also set to address the nation later this evening.

daily.title: Germany: Ex-spy chief sent to pretrial detention on treason charges
daily.summary: August Hanning has been remanded into pretrial detention after his arrest. The case has prompted calls for transparency when spies leave the government.

daily.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
daily.summary: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."

daily.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
daily.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

daily.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
daily.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

daily.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
daily.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

daily.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
daily.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

daily.title: The solar boom is rapidly transforming emerging economies
daily.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. So while the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the poorest countries in the world are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

daily.title: Israel marks third anniversary of October 7 Hamas terror attacks with memorials
daily.summary: Families gathered at the Nova music festival site and other attack locations in memory of those killed by Hamas on October 7, 2023.

daily.title: Yemen's Houthis claim strikes on Aden, Riyadh airports
daily.summary: Aden International Airport came under attack as Yemen's war intensified, with the Houthis targeting key transport hubs.

daily.title: Germany news: Government presents plan for railroad revamp
daily.summary: The Transport Ministry has put forward a five-year plan for improving Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure. Chancellor Merz has voiced solidarity with Israel on the anniversary of the October 7 attacks. DW has more.

daily.title: India news: Opposition protest clouds Modi's 25-year milestone
daily.summary: Delhi police has beefed up security around the Election Commission of India, likely preparing for another day of 'vote theft' protests. Meanwhile, PM Modi marks 25 years in public service. Follow live.

daily.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
daily.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the campaign.

daily.title: Mali: Junta forces retake strategic town of Kidal from separatists
daily.summary: Mali's military regained control of the strategic town of Kidal after forcing Tuareg separatists and al Qaeda-linked jihadists to withdraw following an offensive backed by Russia's Africa Corps.

daily.title: Football: Lionel Messi plays final game for Argentina
daily.summary: Argentinian superstar Lionel Messi bowed out of international football with one last goal for his country. For football in Argentina, and indeed across the world, it's the end of an era.

daily.title: Christa Pike awake after failed Tennessee execution: lawyers
daily.summary: A death row inmate who survived a botched execution last week is conscious and talking in hospital, according to her lawyers, who want to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment without parole.

daily.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
daily.summary: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

daily.title: French AI company announces new, private model
daily.summary: The company's new model, named "Le Chonk," is its first release in five months. Mistral says it outruns some of its Chinese competitors in several areas.

daily.title: Naked Trump statue goes on display in Strasbourg
daily.summary: Titled "The Orange Plague," a gold-coated statue presents Donald Trump sitting on a smaller man's back. The Danish artist blamed Trump for getting in the way of efforts to address climate change.

daily.title: Germany shaken by espionage and treason allegations
daily.summary: The former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, has been accused of spying for a foreign country. Never before has a German official of August Hanning's stature been accused of treason.

daily.title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
daily.summary: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

daily.title: France's conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
daily.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

daily.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
daily.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

daily.title: Germany's far-right AfD makes history again in Saxony-Anhalt
daily.summary: For the first time since the end of World War II, a German state parliament has chosen parliamentary speaker from the far right: Tobias Rausch of the Alternative for Germany (AfD).

daily.title: Nobel Literature Prize: How the winner is secretly chosen
daily.summary: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in Literature?

weekly.title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
weekly.summary: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

weekly.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
weekly.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

weekly.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists
weekly.summary: At a rare public hearing Germany's intelligence agencies identified Russia as the country's most dangerous adversary. The threat from China is also coming into focus. And the homegrown far right also poses a challenge.

weekly.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament
weekly.summary: For the first time since World War II, a far-right party has a house speaker in a German state parliament. And Germany's foreign minister has warned that the climate crisis could fuel extremism.

weekly.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
weekly.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

weekly.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there
weekly.summary: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the countries.

weekly.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
weekly.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

weekly.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?
weekly.summary: Germany's top court, which turned 75 this year, is losing the population's trust, surveys show. Some say reforms in the way it picks candidates would help, to also accept candidates nominated by the far-right AfD.

weekly.title: Germany news: Spy chief warns Russia conflict risk growing
weekly.summary: Moscow is already waging a "shadow war" against Europe, the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service says. The Left Party is taking a case over remarks by the CDU's Katherina Reiche to a top court.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
weekly.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

weekly.title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
weekly.summary: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

weekly.title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
weekly.summary: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

weekly.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
weekly.summary: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

weekly.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
weekly.summary: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

weekly.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
weekly.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

weekly.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity
weekly.summary: A new study highlights persistent structural disparities in wealth and leadership positions between East and West Germany, 36 years after reunification.

weekly.title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
weekly.summary: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

weekly.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
weekly.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

weekly.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
weekly.summary: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.

weekly.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
weekly.summary: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?

weekly.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
weekly.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

weekly.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government
weekly.summary: On the 36th anniversary of reunification, Germans are dissatisfied with the country's political leaders. They don't believe they'll be able to handle the challenges posed by AI, Russia and Donald Trump.

weekly.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
weekly.summary: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

weekly.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
weekly.summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

weekly.title: EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
weekly.summary: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

weekly.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
weekly.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

weekly.title: Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
weekly.summary: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

weekly.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
weekly.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

weekly.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
weekly.summary: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
weekly.summary: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
weekly.summary: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

weekly.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
weekly.summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

weekly.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
weekly.summary: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?

weekly.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
weekly.summary: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

weekly.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
weekly.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

developing.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
developing.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
